comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 (Onderwijs- en Examenregeling bacheloropleiding Fiscaal Recht 2026/2027, article 10, for students starting in September 2026; programme pages and documents checked 2026-10-01)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official Maastricht University programme pages (s0 Vakken & curriculum, s1 programme page, s2 Waarom deze studie, s3 Jouw toekomst) describe the Dutch-taught, full-time, three-year bachelor in Maastricht, whose first year is shared with Rechtsgeleerdheid and which adds national and international tax law to the basic legal subjects (private, administrative, constitutional and criminal law). The Vakken & curriculum page itself only links to the UM course repository, which could not be read without JavaScript, so the 180-EC structure comes from the formally adopted 2026/2027 Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (s4, article 10), which lists every course unit with its EC and code per semester and year. Year 1 totals 60 EC (semester 1: 3 + 10 + 5 + 3 + 6 EC; semester 2: 5 + 6 + 10 + 6 EC; Professionele Vaardigheden jaar 1, 6 EC, over both semesters), year 2 totals 60 EC (semester 3: 7 + 8 + 10 + 2 EC; semester 4: 7 + 7 + 7 + 3 + 3 EC; Professionele Vaardigheden jaar 2, 6 EC, over both semesters) and year 3 totals 60 EC (nine compulsory units including the 10-EC Eindwerkstuk). The programme has no routes, specialisations, restricted choices or free elective space; every unit is compulsory, so no pathway had to be instantiated. The optional Honours programme, which may replace the Eindwerkstuk, and the free education programme of article 47 are not part of the regular pathway and are not reconstructed. Unit content comes from the 2025-2026 Faculty of Law course descriptions (s5), the latest published descriptions; they still list the two Professional Skills units of year 2 at 0 EC, whereas the 2026/2027 OER (s4) gives Professionele Vaardigheden jaar 2 as one 6-EC unit (LPO2100), which is followed here. The OER also names Burgerlijk Procesrecht under two codes (PRI3205 in article 10 and MET2205 in article 21); article 10's code is used. Checked 2026-10-01.

programmes.label: Bachelor Fiscaal Recht at Maastricht University
Closest match to Tax Law: Law, Public Economics and Accounting with Ethics and Argumentation

coreField.label: Dutch tax law: the introduction to tax law (income tax, wage tax, gift tax), personal income tax I and II, cost-price-increasing taxes with the emphasis on VAT, and corporate taxation I and II, which the programme names as its financial subjects alongside the basic legal subjects.

International and European tax law and cross-border taxation: the (Internationaal) Belastingrecht voor Ondernemingen II unit and the EU-harmonised VAT of Kostprijsverhogende belastingen, the programme's international and European dimension and its link to the master International and European Tax Law.

General legal foundations alongside tax law: private law (Inleiding Privaatrecht, Verbintenissenrecht, Goederenrecht, Relatievermogens- en Erfrecht), constitutional and administrative law, criminal law and procedure, international and European law, company and insolvency law, labour law and civil and administrative procedure, which the programme names as the basic subjects that make the tax lawyer broadly employable.

Formal tax law and the rights and duties of taxpayers and tax authorities: Formeel Belastingrecht (the Awb and AWR, the inspector's powers, assessment, burden of proof, appeal, collection, fiscal fines and their limits with criminal prosecution under the ECHR) and the fundamental-rights part of Fiscale Ethiek en Grondrechten.

Foundations, justification and ethics of taxation: Grondslagen en Methoden van Belastingrecht (why taxes exist, whether taxation can be justified, how a tax system can contribute to a just society and a healthy economy, assessed from legal-theoretical and economic foundations) and the ethical dilemmas of government, citizen and adviser in Fiscale Ethiek en Grondrechten.

Business economics and annual accounts for tax lawyers: Bedrijfseconomie (preparing, valuing and analysing the annual accounts, the relation between the commercial and the fiscal annual accounts, and corporate and income tax in the accounts) and the company law of Ondernemings- en Faillissementsrecht.

Legal method, interpretation of legislation and independent research: Juridische Vaardigheden I and II (legal analysis, case solving, source research in legislation, case law and literature, comparing legal systems, a limited legal research paper), the research training of Grondslagen en Methoden van Belastingrecht and the individually written Eindwerkstuk.

Professional legal skills: written and oral argumentation, drafting letters, advice and procedural documents, intake interviews, negotiation, pleading and debate, and the portfolio-based Professionele Vaardigheden units in years 1 and 2.

adjacentDirections.label: Taxation, public finance and the wider societal effects of tax: how taxes fund public services and how tax systems relate to economic inequality, health, the environment and mobility, a theme the programme raises in its foundations unit and its pages on why taxation matters.

questionsApplications.label: Why do states levy taxes, can taxation be justified, and how should a tax system be designed so that it contributes to a just society and a healthy economy?
How are the rights and duties of taxpayers balanced against the powers of the tax authorities, and what do ethics and fundamental rights require of government, citizens and advisers?
How are tax rules interpreted and applied to real cases of individuals, businesses and cross-border activity, and how is the outcome argued and explained in advice?

alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response to the Bachelor Fiscaal Recht at Maastricht University, which combines the basic legal subjects (private, constitutional and administrative, criminal, international and European law) with national and international tax law, formal tax procedure, the foundations and ethics of taxation, business economics and annual accounts, legal method and a bachelor thesis. UCR has no tax-law course, no Dutch-law curriculum and no procedural-law courses, so this programme cannot reproduce the tax-law core. It instead builds on what UCR genuinely offers: the general legal foundations in its law courses (private, constitutional, criminal, international, EU, business and human-rights law), the economics of taxation and public spending (Public Economics with the macro- and microeconomics around it), accounting and finance for the business-economics component, ethics and political philosophy for the fairness and justification of taxation, and argumentation, negotiation and research skills for the legal-skills strand. It offers related disciplinary perspectives on taxation and does not teach tax law.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has eight law courses (Law, Society & Justice, Principles of Private Law, Comparative Constitutional Law, Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, Introduction to Public International Law, Foundations of European Union Law, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy and Transnational Business Law), five economics courses (Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics and Econometrics), two accounting and finance courses and one international business course (Accounting & Corporate Finance, Money, Banking & Finance, International Business & Governance), Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Ethics, Introduction to Political Philosophy and European Union Politics, and argumentation and research skills (Research Methods & Statistics, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, The Art of Rhetorical Communication), together with Personal & Professional Development. The label names the law, public economics and accounting that dominate it and its ethics and argumentation strands, and it does not suggest a tax-law major, which UCR does not offer: no UCR course teaches tax law.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Every formal prerequisite is scheduled in an earlier semester: Law, Society & Justice and Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations in semester 1 precede Foundations of European Union Law, Comparative Constitutional Law, Principles of Private Law, Criminal Law & Criminal Justice and Introduction to Public International Law (Law, Society & Justice) and Transnational Business Law, International Business & Governance and Money, Banking & Finance (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations); Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 precedes International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, Econometrics and Negotiation & Strategic Thinking. Every course is placed in a semester in which it is planned. Advisory progression is respected where the planned semesters allow: Introduction to Economics opens the economics line in semester 1 before International Macroeconomics (semester 3) and the 300-level Public Economics (semester 4, its only planned semester); the general law course and the rhetoric skills course open the programme; the introductory political philosophy course precedes European Union Politics; and Ethics and the 300-level finance and econometrics courses come last. Microeconomics & Behavior and Public Economics share semester 4 because Public Economics is offered only then and Microeconomics & Behavior requires Research Methods & Statistics first.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One UCR alternative is defensible and production stopped at one. Alternative 1 owns six generator-eligible rows as the target's own core: 5903 (Dutch tax law) and 5900 (how tax law affects people, businesses and society), which the programme addresses through its tax-law units that UCR cannot teach and which Alternative 1 therefore approaches only through general law, taxation economics and accounting; 5904 and 5908 (international and European tax law, cross-border taxation), approached through public international law, EU law, Transnational Business Law and International Business & Governance; and 5913 and 5914 (rights and duties of taxpayers and tax authorities, interpreting and applying legislation), approached through constitutional, criminal and human-rights law and the law foundation course. Two candidate directions were assessed and rejected. Taxation, public finance, ethics and fairness (5901 and 5902, supported by 5900) is coherent and evidenced by the programme's own foundations unit, but the UCR courses that implement it are exactly Public Economics, International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Introduction to Economics, Ethics, Introduction to Political Philosophy and Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, which Alternative 1 already contains; a second programme could only reuse them and fill the remaining slots with courses that have no demonstrated link to taxation or public spending, so no substantively different curriculum follows and the candidate is rejected as not-substantively-distinct. Legal practice, solving cases, drafting advice and independent legal research (5915, 5916, 5917 and 5919) is evidenced by the programme's skills units, but UCR has no legal-practice, drafting or case-solving courses; the only relevant content is the moot court and legal aid clinic simulation inside Law, Society & Justice and Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, and the rhetoric, negotiation and research-methods courses, all of which Alternative 1 already includes, so this candidate too is rejected as not-substantively-distinct and not as arbitrary substitution. The remaining generator-eligible rows are all accounted for above, and the curricular topics (5905 to 5907 and 5909 to 5912 and 5918) only support the core, the interests about careers and professions (5920 to 5926) are search-only and generate nothing.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce what law is, its functions and its relation to society and the state: the Maastricht unit studies the binding force of law, the structure of a legal system, natural-law and positivist approaches, the rule of law and the separation of powers, and the aims of the main fields of law, while Law, Society & Justice explores definitions of law, legal traditions, the fields of law and the relation between law and society and justice. The Maastricht unit is a shorter philosophical introduction, so scope differs.

Both study the core of private law: Inleiding Privaatrecht covers the law of obligations (contract, tort, unjust enrichment) and property law under Dutch civil law, while Principles of Private Law examines property, tort and contract law comparatively, so the Dutch statutory basis and the depth differ.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Verbintenissenrecht deepens the Dutch law of obligations; the one UCR private-law course is already placed with Inleiding Privaatrecht, and no other UCR course addresses obligations at this depth.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Goederenrecht is the Dutch law of property and security rights; the only UCR course touching property law is already placed with Inleiding Privaatrecht and is not a specialist counterpart.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Relatievermogensrecht en Erfrecht (matrimonial property and succession law) has no UCR counterpart.

Both address the legal organisation of business: Ondernemings- en Faillissementsrecht covers the legal forms of enterprises, their formation, management and representation, directors' liability and dissolution, and Transnational Business Law surveys company law and contracts law across legal systems. Insolvency law is not covered at UCR and the UCR course is transnational rather than Dutch, so scope differs.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Arbeidsrecht (Dutch employment law) has no UCR counterpart.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Burgerlijk Procesrecht (civil procedure) has no UCR counterpart; the moot court in Law, Society & Justice is a trial simulation and not a procedural-law course.

Both study the constitutional state: Inleiding Staatsrecht covers democracy, the rule of law, the Constitution, the separation of powers, the relation between government and parliament and the legality principle, while Comparative Constitutional Law covers constitutionalism, the separation of powers, judicial review and fundamental rights. The UCR course is comparative and not Dutch.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Inleiding Bestuursrecht is the Dutch general administrative law (Awb, decisions, administrative bodies, principles of good administration); Comparative Constitutional Law touches administrative law but is placed with the constitutional-law unit that it matches more directly.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Bestuursprocesrecht (administrative procedure) has no UCR counterpart.

Both examine the foundations of criminal law: Inleiding Straf- en Strafprocesrecht covers substantive criminal law and criminal procedure, while Criminal Law & Criminal Justice covers criminal accountability, guilt, justifications and excuses, the legality principle, the presumption of innocence and the justification of punishment. UCR does not cover criminal procedure.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Straf- en Strafprocesrecht is the advanced Dutch continuation of the first-year unit; the one UCR criminal-law course is placed with the introductory unit and is not an advanced or procedural counterpart.

Both introduce public international law: Inleiding Internationaal en Europees Recht covers the sources and subjects of international law, international organisations such as the UN, treaties, dispute settlement and compliance, and Introduction to Public International Law covers sources, subjects and organisation, the use of force, treaties, refugee and environmental law and treaty negotiation and compliance. The Maastricht unit also covers European law, which the UCR course does not.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Inleiding Belastingrecht introduces Dutch income, wage and gift tax and formal tax law; UCR has no course on tax law, and Public Economics, which treats taxation economically, is placed with the unit on the foundations of taxation.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Belastingrecht voor Particulieren I (Dutch personal income tax law) has no UCR counterpart.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Formeel Belastingrecht (tax procedure, the powers of the inspector, collection and fiscal fines) has no UCR counterpart; Comparative Constitutional Law and Criminal Law & Criminal Justice give only general legal background.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Belastingrecht voor Particulieren II (Dutch personal income tax law, advanced) has no UCR counterpart.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Kostprijsverhogende belastingen (VAT, excise and other taxes that raise cost prices, largely governed by EU law) has no UCR counterpart; Foundations of European Union Law covers the EU legal order and internal market but no tax law.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Belastingrecht voor Ondernemingen I (Dutch corporate taxation) has no UCR counterpart.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: (Internationaal) Belastingrecht voor Ondernemingen II (international corporate taxation) has no UCR counterpart; Transnational Business Law and International Business & Governance give only general cross-border business context.

Both address the economic grounds of taxation: Grondslagen en Methoden van Belastingrecht studies the legal-theoretical and economic foundations of taxation and asks how a tax system can contribute to a just society and a healthy economy, while Public Economics covers the role of government, taxation, public goods, externalities, public spending and redistribution and the effect of policy on efficiency and equity. The Maastricht unit also covers legal theory and tax-law research methods, which the UCR course does not.

Both address the ethics of public authority and citizens: Fiscale Ethiek en Grondrechten applies ethical reasoning to dilemmas of government, taxpayer and adviser and covers fundamental rights from a fiscal perspective, while Ethics covers moral reasoning and practical ethics including equality, poverty and wealth. The UCR course is general and does not treat tax dilemmas or constitutional review.

Both teach the preparation and analysis of annual accounts: Bedrijfseconomie covers the content and preparation of the annual accounts, valuing its items and ratio analysis, and Accounting & Corporate Finance covers accounting theory and practice and the analysis of financial statements. The Maastricht unit also covers fiscal accounting and the processing of income and corporate tax in the accounts, which the UCR course does not.

Both are first-years' units in personal and professional development: Professionele Vaardigheden jaar 1 develops academic skills, collaboration, communication, feedback and self-regulation through a portfolio and reflection with a coach, and Personal & Professional Development stimulates personal development and academic skills and ethical orientation. The Maastricht unit is geared to future legal professionals.

Both train structured written and oral argumentation: Juridische Vaardigheden I teaches analytical, written and oral skills including a legal argument, a presentation and a plea, and The Art of Rhetorical Communication trains structuring persuasive arguments for essays and oral presentations. The Maastricht unit works with statutes, case law and legal document types, which the UCR course does not.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Juridische Vaardigheden II (source research in legislation, case law and literature, comparison of legal systems, a limited legal research paper, debating and pleading) has no UCR counterpart; the one UCR rhetoric course is already placed with Juridische Vaardigheden I, and the research-methods course is empirical, not legal.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Professionele Vaardigheden jaar 2 continues the portfolio-based professional development of the programme and has no second UCR counterpart beyond Personal & Professional Development, already placed with the first-year unit.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the Eindwerkstuk is an individual legal research thesis; Research Methods & Statistics trains empirical research and is not a counterpart, and UCR's optional independent research is shown opposite it.

notes.text: The Bachelor Fiscaal Recht combines national and international tax law, formal tax procedure, the foundations and ethics of taxation and business economics with the basic subjects of Dutch law. At UCR, students can approach taxation through fields such as law, public economics, accounting and finance, ethics and political philosophy. These programmes therefore offer related perspectives rather than reproducing a full tax-law curriculum.

Both programmes include substantial study of law and the economics of public finance. The Bachelor Fiscaal Recht additionally includes specialist work in Dutch income, wage, corporate and value-added taxation, international taxation, formal tax procedure and Dutch civil, administrative and criminal procedure. UCR students can instead combine general law courses with public economics, accounting and ethics, but those specialist components are not offered at the same level of depth.
